title: Tour de France Femmes 2027: London to host first team time trial in race history
content:
London will host the first team time trial in Tour de France Femmes (TdFF) history in the final stage of the 2027 Grand Depart.

The 18-kilometer circuit will take riders past the Houses of Parliament, London Eye and Tower Bridge before finishing on the Mall on August 1, 2027, race organisers announced on Monday.

The team discipline has been increasingly rare, with the Vuelta Feminina the only Grand Tour last year hosting one, and none of the Spanish stage race, the TdFF or the women’s Giro d’Italia opting for a team time trial (TTT) in 2026.

It is also the first time that the TdFF has come to the United Kingdom, and the first time that the Tour’s men’s and women’s races host their Grands Depart outside of France in the same country.

Expanding the details of the 2027 Tour in London on Monday, race organisers revealed the profile of the first two days of racing — including what director Marion Rousse called one of the “hardest race stages ever in a Grand Depart” — before the peloton reaches the capital.

The first day is set to span 86km from Leeds — where the men’s race started in 2014 — to Manchester, taking in three climbs that could split up the peloton in what is expected to be a sprint stage.

“On paper it looks fairly easy but it will be short, dynamic and tough,” Rousse told a press briefing on Monday.

The second stage, however, will host around 3,000 metres of climbing across 154.4km from Manchester to Sheffield.

“It will be very, very, very hard,” Rousse continued. “There is not one single flat kilometer, this will be a battle, it will be hard fought. The three stages will be harder than they seem, it is a hugely historic moment for the TdFF and the race as a whole.”

Movistar’s Cat Ferguson, 19, called the chance to make history on her home roads an “honour”.

“Arguably we are going to the two most iconic places in the UK — Yorkshire and London,” the five-time junior world champion said on Monday.

“The amount of people that came out to watch in (2014) … the support that the British people show is like nothing else, it’s such an honour.

“If I can inspire some women or young girls, even in a small way, to get out on their bikes, that would make me very happy. Bring on the 2027 Grand Depart.”
